title: Polynomial associated graded structure after quotienting by an initial segment
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $b\geq0$, and let $f_1,\ldots,f_b\in A$. Put $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_b)$ and $C=A/J$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Suppose that the canonical graded $C$-algebra homomorphism
$$C[T_1,\ldots,T_b]\longrightarrow\operatorname{gr}_J(A),\qquad T_j\longmapsto[f_j]_1,$$
is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. For every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq b$, put $I_i=(f_1,\ldots,f_i)$ (with $I_0=0$), $B_i=A/I_i$, and $\overline J_i=(\overline f_{i+1},\ldots,\overline f_b)\subseteq B_i$, where $\overline f_j$ denotes the image of $f_j$ in $B_i$. Identify $B_i/\overline J_i$ with $C$ by the map induced by $a\mapsto a\bmod J$. Then the canonical graded $C$-algebra homomorphism
$$C[T_{i+1},\ldots,T_b]\longrightarrow\operatorname{gr}_{\overline J_i}(B_i),\qquad T_j\longmapsto[\overline f_j]_1,$$
is an isomorphism. Polynomial rings on no variables mean $C$.

source.place: Tag 061R, lemma-truncate-quasi-regular, specialized to M=A; Tag 061P, definition-quasi-regular-sequence, and Tag 061N, equation-quasi-regular, expand the quasi-regular hypothesis and conclusion.

proof.text: Write Phi_f for the canonical evaluation map. By induction on monomials, the product and scalar formulas for associated graded classes identify Phi_f(map(A -> A/J)(P)) with the degree-n class of P(f), for a homogeneous degree-n polynomial P over A. Lifting coefficients and taking homogeneous components then shows that injectivity of Phi_f implies: P(f) in J^(n+1) forces every coefficient of P into J. Conversely this coefficient criterion proves injectivity by homogeneous components, and expanding ideal powers by homogeneous polynomials proves surjectivity. A zero-relation version of the criterion suffices: expand an element of J^(n+1) in degree n with coefficients in J, subtract that expansion, and apply the zero-relation criterion.

source.place: Tag 061R, lemma-truncate-quasi-regular, specialized to M=A; Tag 061P, definition-quasi-regular-sequence, and Tag 061N, equation-quasi-regular, expand the quasi-regular hypothesis and conclusion.

proof.text: For a chosen generator t=f_j, prove t*y in J^(n+1) implies y in J^n by induction on n. At n=0 the assertion is automatic. In the induction step the preceding assertion puts y in J^(n-1); expand y=P(f) homogeneously in degree n-1. Apply the coefficient criterion to X_j*P, whose evaluation lies in J^(n+1), to put every coefficient of P in J (compare coefficients at e_j+d). Expand those coefficients in the generators of J to raise P to degree n with the same evaluation. This is the finite filtration argument of Stacks 061R and requires no separatedness.

source.place: Tag 061R, lemma-truncate-quasi-regular, specialized to M=A; Tag 061P, definition-quasi-regular-sequence, and Tag 061N, equation-quasi-regular, expand the quasi-regular hypothesis and conclusion.

proof.text: Let q:A -> B be surjective with kernel (f_j), and let g be the images of the other generators, indexed injectively by variables different from j, generating q(J). For a homogeneous zero relation p(g)=0, lift its coefficients to A and take the same homogeneous component, obtaining P; rename its variables to obtain H. Then H(f)=t*y. In degree n>=1, the preceding filtration assertion gives y in J^(n-1), so choose a homogeneous Q of degree n-1 evaluating to y. The homogeneous zero relation H-X_j*Q has all coefficients in J by Step 1. At a monomial supported on the remaining variables, the X_j*Q coefficient is zero, so the original coefficients of P lie in J; their images are in q(J). At degree zero H(f) lies in (t) subset J directly. Step 1 now proves bijectivity of Phi_g. The same coefficient-lifting argument, without subtracting X_j*Q, transports the criterion across a bijective ring map.

source.place: Tag 061R, lemma-truncate-quasi-regular, specialized to M=A; Tag 061P, definition-quasi-regular-sequence, and Tag 061N, equation-quasi-regular, expand the quasi-regular hypothesis and conclusion.

proof.text: For I_i=span(f_j : j<i), prove I_i<=J and map(A -> A/I_i)(J)=span(g_i). Also I_(i+1)=I_i+(f_i). Therefore the surjective factor A/I_i -> A/I_(i+1) has kernel generated by the image of f_i and carries the remaining ideal to the next remaining ideal. The inclusion of the next tail index into the present tail is injective and omits i. Apply Step 3. The initial case i=0 follows by transporting across A -> A/0. Induction proves bijectivity for every i<=b, including b=0 and the empty tail at i=b. Finally the third isomorphism theorem, using I_i<=J and the image-ideal identity, gives (A/I_i)/span(g_i) equiv A/J. Its representative formula sends the double class of a to the class of a.
